findings.title: Turn 4 violates D-000's mandatory three-turn termination
findings.charge: D-000 permits three exchanges per party. With no consensus after turn 3, it requires the decision to be recorded CONTESTED and parked for the user; a forced consensus may never be recorded as consensus. D-272 had no consensus at turn 1, turn 2 was Dual OBJECT, and turn 3 was Dual OBJECT. The subject nevertheless calls itself 'D-000 new cycle, turn 4 of 3' and remains an adoption candidate.
evidence: Live COORD D-000 clause 2 says: termination after 3 turns each side; if no consensus, record CONTESTED, park for the user, and never record forced consensus as consensus.
The frozen reviews establish turn 1 Split, turn 2 Dual OBJECT, and turn 3 Dual OBJECT.
The subject's literal 'turn 4 of 3' is internally impossible and is not a new cycle: it retains D-272, carries turns 1-3 as predecessors, and labels this exchange turn 4.
Established COORD handling records exhausted cycles CONTESTED and starts any retry as turn 1 of a new cycle, explicitly 'not turn 4'.
The subject records no direct user-made substantive decision, no explicit amendment or exception to D-000, and no CONTESTED predecessor ledger.
findings.whyMustFix: This is an authority defect, not presentation. A CONSENT here could not lawfully be recorded as delegated D-000 consensus. The current user request authorizes performing the review, but it does not silently rewrite the subject's claimed adoption authority or D-000's frozen termination rule.
findings.repair: Do not adopt D-272 from this fourth exchange under D-000. Record the exhausted D-272 cycle CONTESTED with both turn-3 positions and park it for the user. If the user expressly chooses to continue, either record a direct user-made disposition/explicit protocol exception, or open a separately identified new cycle at turn 1 with the CONTESTED predecessor ledger. Remove 'turn 4 of 3' and do not call any fourth-round result D-000 consensus.
